description: UI Bridge State Machine page — discover, design, and manage state machine configs with states, transitions, graph visualization, pathfinding, and export. Users connect to SDK-enabled apps to discover states via fingerprint-based co-occurrence analysis, then work across six tabs: Discovery (SDK app connection, explore/record data collection with element thumbnail capture, fingerprint-based state discovery, and save), Graph Editor (visual node-edge layout via dagre with drag-and-drop element reassignment and element thumbnail display), State View (list + detail panel via shared StateViewPanel), Transitions (list with detail panel via shared TransitionsPanel), Pathfinding (find optimal paths between states via shared PathfindingPanel), and Export (save to JSON file or load into runtime).

groups.name: Page Header and Config Selector
groups.description: The page header shows a Network icon and a dynamic title (the active config name, or 'UI Bridge States' when no config is selected). When element thumbnails are loaded, the title appends '[Nt]' showing the count. A config selector dropdown lets users pick an existing config (showing name and render count). A Refresh button reloads configs and active data, showing a spinning animation during loading.

assertions.description: The page displays 'UI Bridge States' as the default title when no config is selected, or the active config name when one is loaded
A config selector dropdown with a 'Select configuration...' placeholder option lets users choose which state machine config to work with. Each option shows the config name and render count.
A 'Refresh' button reloads configs and the active config data. The RefreshCw icon animates (spins) while loading is in progress.
When element thumbnails are loaded for the active config, the title appends a count like '[5t]' showing how many thumbnails are available
assertions.expected: When thumbnails are loaded, the h1 title should contain text matching the pattern '[Nt]' where N is the number of thumbnails (e.g., '[12t]'). When no thumbnails, no bracket suffix appears.
preconditions: A config is selected with saved element thumbnails

groups.name: Tab Navigation Bar
groups.description: Six tabs appear below the header (always visible, regardless of config selection): Discovery, Graph Editor, State View, Transitions, Pathfinding, and Export. The active tab is highlighted with background and shadow styling. Each tab has an icon and label. Discovery is the default active tab.

assertions.description: The Discovery tab provides access to the SDK connection and state discovery workflow
The Graph Editor tab provides access to the interactive dagre-based node-edge visualization of states and transitions
The State View tab shows all states with a list and detail panel layout
The Transitions tab lists all transitions between states with editing support
The Pathfinding tab enables users to find optimal paths between states
The Export tab provides JSON file save and load operations for state machine configs
Exactly 6 tabs are rendered in the tab bar
assertions.expected: The tab bar section below the header should contain exactly 6 tab buttons: Discovery, Graph Editor, State View, Transitions, Pathfinding, Export

groups.name: Per-Tab Empty States (No Config Selected)
groups.description: When no config is selected, each content tab (Graph Editor, State View, Transitions, Pathfinding, Export) shows a centered text message instructing the user to select a configuration. The Discovery tab does not show this message as it works independently of config selection.

assertions.description: The Graph Editor tab shows 'Select a configuration to view the state graph' when no config is selected

criteria.textContent: Select a configuration to view the state graph

assertions.description: The State View tab shows 'Select a configuration to view states' when no config is selected

criteria.textContent: Select a configuration to view states

assertions.description: The Transitions tab shows 'Select a configuration to view transitions' when no config is selected

criteria.textContent: Select a configuration to view transitions

assertions.description: The Pathfinding tab shows 'Select a configuration to use pathfinding' when no config is selected

criteria.textContent: Select a configuration to use pathfinding

assertions.description: The Export tab shows 'Select a configuration to export' when no config is selected

groups.name: Discovery Phase 1: Connect to SDK App
groups.description: The first phase of the discovery workflow shows a connection card with a Plug icon and 'Connect to SDK App' label. Users click 'Scan for Apps' to discover SDK-enabled apps (web and desktop). Found apps are listed with name, URL, framework, and a 'Connect' button. When connected, a green banner shows 'Connected: [App Name]'. Auto-scans on mount if no apps found.

assertions.description: The connection card shows 'Connect to SDK App' as its heading
A 'Scan for Apps' button triggers discovery of SDK-enabled apps. Shows a Loader2 spinner while scanning and is disabled during scan.
After scanning, a text shows the count of discovered apps (e.g., '3 apps found')
assertions.expected: Each discovered app card shows: app name (font-medium), URL and framework in text-muted, and a 'Connect' button (brand-primary background). After connecting, the app list is hidden and replaced by a connected banner.

assertions.description: When connected to an SDK app, a green-tinted banner shows 'Connected: [App Name]' with a CheckCircle2 icon
assertions.expected: A banner with green background (bg-green-500/10) and green border should display 'Connected: <app name>' with a green CheckCircle2 icon when an SDK connection is active

assertions.description: Discovered apps are shown in a list with app name, URL, framework info, and a 'Connect' button for each. The app list is hidden once connected.
assertions.expected: Each discovered app should show: (1) app name in bold, (2) URL and framework in muted text, (3) a brand-primary 'Connect' button. Clicking Connect establishes an SDK connection. The app list is hidden once connected.
preconditions: Scan found at least one app

assertions.description: When no apps are found and not scanning, instructional text says 'Click Scan to find apps with the UI Bridge SDK installed.'

criteria.textContent: Click Scan to find apps with the UI Bridge SDK installed.

groups.name: Discovery Phase 2: Collect Data — Explore Tab
groups.description: When connected, two sub-tabs appear: Explore and Record. The Explore tab provides automated exploration of the connected app. A 'Start Exploration' button triggers automated element interaction. During exploration, a Cancel button appears, and progress shows current/total interactions and the current element being explored.

assertions.description: An 'Explore' sub-tab button is available when connected to an SDK app
A 'Record' sub-tab with a Camera icon is available for manual capture sessions
A 'Start Exploration' button triggers automated state exploration. Shows Compass icon normally, Loader2 spinner while exploring, and text changes to 'Exploring...' during active exploration.
assertions.expected: Clicking 'Start Exploration' begins automated exploration. The button text changes to 'Exploring...' with a Loader2 spinner and becomes disabled. A 'Cancel' button appears alongside. Progress text shows 'Progress: X / Y interactions' and 'Current: <element name>'. When exploration completes, co-occurrence data is stored and the view advances to Phase 3.

assertions.description: A 'Cancel' button appears during exploration and is hidden otherwise
assertions.expected: A 'Cancel' button with border styling should appear next to the exploration button only while exploration is in progress. When not exploring, this button is hidden.

assertions.description: During exploration, progress text shows 'Progress: X / Y interactions' and optionally 'Current: [element name]'
assertions.expected: When exploration is active, text should show 'Progress: N / M interactions' where N is current count and M is total. Below that, 'Current: [element identifier]' shows which element is being explored.

groups.name: Discovery Phase 2: Collect Data — Record Tab
groups.description: The Record tab allows manual capture session recording. Users click 'Start Recording' (red circle icon) to begin, and 'Stop Recording' (square icon) to end. During recording, a pulsing red dot and capture count badge appear. After stopping, the co-occurrence data is generated from recorded captures.

assertions.description: A 'Record' sub-tab button with Camera icon is available when connected
A 'Start Recording' button with a red Circle icon begins a capture session. Hidden while recording is active.
assertions.expected: Initially shows 'Start Recording' button with a red Circle icon. When recording, the button changes to 'Stop Recording' (red background, Square icon). A recording status area shows: a red pulsing dot with 'N captures' badge, and 'N unique fingerprints' text. Stopping recording generates co-occurrence export data and advances to Phase 3.

assertions.description: A 'Stop Recording' button with Square icon (red bg) appears during active recording and is hidden otherwise
assertions.expected: Automatically explore

groups.name: Discovery Phase 3: Discover States from Co-occurrence Data
groups.description: After collecting co-occurrence data (via Explore or Record), a summary card shows 'Co-occurrence Data Collected' with capture count, fingerprint count, and data source badge. A 'Start Over' button resets. A 'Discover States' button runs fingerprint-based state discovery via the Rust backend (with JS fallback).

assertions.description: The co-occurrence data summary shows 'Co-occurrence Data Collected' heading with Layers icon
The data summary shows badges for captures count, fingerprints count, and data source (explore/record)
assertions.expected: Three inline badges should show: (1) 'N captures' with Hash icon, (2) 'M fingerprints', (3) 'via explore' or 'via record' capitalized. All in pill-shaped badges.

assertions.description: A 'Start Over' button with RotateCcw icon resets all discovery state and returns to Phase 1
A 'Discover States' button with Sparkles icon runs fingerprint-based state discovery. Shows Loader2 spinner while discovering. Disabled during discovery.
preconditions: Discovery has not been run yet

assertions.description: The fingerprint discovery algorithm groups element fingerprints by co-occurrence patterns. It identifies global fingerprints (>80% appearance rate, e.g., header/footer), groups remaining fingerprints by position zone and landmark context, and creates states from each group with computed confidence scores.
assertions.expected: A card with green CheckCircle2 icon and 'Discovery Complete' heading should display: three badges showing 'N states', 'N fingerprints', 'N captures'. Below, a scrollable list (max-h-40) shows each state with its name on the left and 'X% confidence' on the right.

assertions.description: A 'Configuration Name' labeled input with placeholder 'e.g., My App States' allows naming the config before saving

A 'Save Configuration' button saves the discovered states as a new config. Disabled when the name is empty or saving is in progress. On success, switches to Graph Editor tab with the new config loaded.
assertions.expected: Clicking 'Save Configuration' calls discovery.saveConfig() which creates a new state machine config from the discovered states. The button is disabled (opacity-50) when the config name is empty or while saving. On success, the page switches to the Graph Editor tab with the newly created config loaded and selected.

groups.name: Discovery Phase 4: Save Configuration
groups.description: After state discovery completes, a results card shows 'Discovery Complete' with green CheckCircle2, statistics (states, fingerprints, captures), a scrollable state preview list with confidence percentages, a Configuration Name input, and a 'Save Configuration' button.

assertions.description: The discovery results card shows 'Discovery Complete' heading with green CheckCircle2 icon
Statistics badges show the number of discovered states, unique fingerprints, and total captures
assertions.expected: Three badge pills should show: 'N states', 'M fingerprints', 'P captures' representing the discovery result counts

assertions.description: A scrollable state preview list shows each discovered state with its name and confidence percentage
assertions.expected: A bordered, scrollable container (max-h-40) should list each discovered state with: state name on the left and 'N% confidence' on the right in muted text

assertions.description: A 'Configuration Name' labeled input with placeholder 'e.g., My App States' allows naming the config before saving
A full-width 'Save Configuration' button with Save icon saves the discovered states as a new config. Disabled when name is empty or save is in progress (shows Loader2 spinner).

Clicking Save Configuration creates a new config via sm_create_config, creates all discovered states via sm_create_state, saves element thumbnails via sm_save_thumbnails, then switches to the Graph Editor tab with the new config selected
assertions.expected: After clicking Save Configuration with a valid name: (1) the config and states are persisted to the database, (2) element thumbnails are saved, (3) the page switches to the Graph Editor tab, (4) the new config is automatically selected in the dropdown, (5) a success toast appears. If save fails, an error toast is shown.

groups.name: Graph Editor Tab Content
groups.description: The Graph Editor tab renders an interactive node-edge graph using @xyflow/react with dagre layout. States are nodes and transitions are edges. A floating 'Add Transition' button in the top-left allows creating new transitions. Clicking a node selects that state and opens the state detail panel; clicking an edge selects the transition and opens the transition editor. Supports element drag-and-drop for reassigning elements between states. Element thumbnails are displayed on nodes when available.

assertions.description: A floating 'Add Transition' button with Plus icon in the top-left of the graph allows creating new transitions
When no states exist, the graph shows 'No states discovered yet. Use the Discovery tab to discover states.'
assertions.expected: When a config is selected but has zero states, the graph area should display the instructional message 'No states discovered yet. Use the Discovery tab to discover states.'
preconditions: A config is selected with zero states

assertions.description: Clicking a state node in the graph selects it and opens the state detail panel in the right sidebar, deselecting any previously selected transition
assertions.expected: Clicking a state node should: (1) highlight the node, (2) open the StateDetailPanel in the right side panel showing 'State Details' header, (3) deselect any previously selected transition and close the transition editor
preconditions: A config is selected with at least one state

assertions.description: Clicking a transition edge in the graph selects it and opens the TransitionEditor in the right sidebar
assertions.expected: Clicking a transition edge should: (1) select the edge, (2) open the TransitionEditor in the right side panel in edit mode showing 'Edit Transition' header, (3) deselect any previously selected state
preconditions: A config is selected with at least one transition

assertions.description: When element thumbnails are available, graph nodes display visual representations of the UI elements in each state
assertions.expected: Dragging an element tile from one state node to another should: without Alt key, create a new transition between the two states; with Alt key held, move the element from the source state to the target state. Drop targets are highlighted during drag.
preconditions: A config is selected with at least two states

assertions.description: Elements can be dragged between state nodes to reassign them. Alt+Drag initiates element movement; drop targets highlight during drag.
assertions.expected: Users can Alt+Drag an element from one state node to another to reassign it. During drag, potential drop target states are visually highlighted (dropTargetStateId). On drop, the element is removed from the source state and added to the target state via sm_update_state.
preconditions: Config selected with multiple states having elements

groups.name: Graph Visualization Controls
groups.description: The graph canvas has control buttons (Fit, keyboard shortcut toggle, Re-layout), a stats panel (state count, transition count, initial state), a MiniMap, and keyboard shortcuts. Nodes display element grids, badges (START, outgoing/incoming counts), and confidence indicators.

assertions.description: A 'Fit' button in the graph controls panel adjusts the viewport to show all nodes
assertions.expected: The graph canvas should have a 'Fit' button (with Maximize icon) in the controls panel that fits all nodes into view when clicked
preconditions: A config is selected with states

assertions.description: A 'Re-layout' button in the graph controls re-runs the dagre automatic layout algorithm
assertions.expected: The graph controls panel should include a Re-layout button (with LayoutGrid icon) that recalculates node positions using dagre layout
preconditions: A config is selected with states

assertions.description: A '?' button toggles a keyboard shortcuts overlay showing available graph shortcuts
assertions.expected: After clicking the '?' button, a 'Keyboard Shortcuts' overlay should appear listing available shortcuts: Esc (deselect), F (fit), L (re-layout), +/- (zoom), Tab (cycle states), I (jump to initial), Delete (delete transition)

assertions.description: State nodes in the graph display contextual badges: 'START' for initial states, outgoing/incoming transition counts, and a 'no links' badge for disconnected states
assertions.expected: State nodes should show a gold 'START' badge on initial states, an outgoing count badge (top-right), an incoming count badge (bottom-right), and a 'no links' badge on disconnected states. Each node also shows element count and confidence percentage.
preconditions: A config is selected with states

assertions.description: Transition edges display inline labels with the transition name, action type icons, action count, and path cost
assertions.expected: Each transition edge should render a pill-shaped label showing: action type icons (first 3 unique types, color-coded), transition name (truncated), path cost (if != 1.0), action count badge (if > 1), and a green Eye icon if the transition stays visible
preconditions: A config is selected with transitions

groups.name: Sidebar: State Detail Panel
groups.description: When a state is selected in the Graph Editor, the right sidebar (w-80) shows the shared StateDetailPanel component with editable name, description, metadata grid (state ID, confidence, element count, render count), element list with type-colored badges, and save/delete actions.

assertions.description: The state detail panel shows an editable Name input field pre-filled with the selected state's name
assertions.expected: An editable Name text input should be pre-filled with the current state's name, allowing the user to rename the state
preconditions: A state is selected in Graph Editor

assertions.description: The state detail panel displays a metadata grid showing State ID, Confidence percentage, Elements count, and Renders count
assertions.expected: A metadata grid should display: State ID (monospace), Confidence (color-coded: green >= 80%, amber 50-79%, red < 50%), Elements count, and Renders count

assertions.description: The state detail panel shows an Elements list with type-colored badges and the ability to add/remove elements
assertions.expected: An Elements section should list each element with a type-colored badge (testid: blue, role: green, text: amber, ui: purple, url/nav: cyan). Users can remove elements (x button) and add new elements using a 'type:element-id' input with an Add button.
preconditions: A state is selected with elements

assertions.description: The state detail panel provides 'Save Changes' and 'Delete State' buttons
assertions.expected: A 'Save Changes' button (brand-primary, shown only when changes exist) persists edits via sm_update_state. A 'Delete State' button (red border) removes the state via sm_delete_state.

assertions.description: The state detail sidebar can be closed, deselecting the state
assertions.expected: Clicking the close button on the StateDetailPanel should close the sidebar and deselect the state (setSelectedStateId(null))

groups.name: Sidebar: Transition Editor
groups.description: When a transition is selected or 'Add Transition' is clicked in the Graph Editor, the right sidebar shows the shared TransitionEditor component. It provides state toggle groups (From, Activate, Exit), name input, action list with type-specific fields, path cost, stays-visible checkbox, and create/update/delete buttons.

assertions.description: The transition editor shows three state toggle groups: 'From States' (blue), 'Activate States' (green), and 'Exit States' (red)
assertions.expected: Three labeled toggle groups should be visible: 'From States' (blue accent), 'Activate States' (green accent), and 'Exit States' (red accent). Each group shows state names as toggleable buttons that highlight when selected.
preconditions: Transition editor is open (new or existing)

assertions.description: The transition editor has an Actions section with '+ Add Action' button and action fields with type dropdown and type-specific parameter fields
assertions.expected: An 'Actions' section should show: '+ Add Action' button, and for each action: a type dropdown (click, doubleClick, type, navigate, wait, select, scroll, drag, etc.) with conditional fields (target element ID for click actions, text field for type actions, URL for navigate, delay for wait, etc.)

assertions.description: The transition editor has 'Path Cost' number input and 'Stays Visible' checkbox options
assertions.expected: A 'Path Cost' number input (min 0, step 0.1) and a 'Stays Visible' checkbox should be present at the bottom of the transition editor

assertions.description: The transition editor has a 'Create' button (new mode) or 'Update' button (edit mode) and a 'Delete' button (edit mode only)
assertions.expected: In create mode: a 'Create' button (brand-primary). In edit mode: an 'Update' button (brand-primary) and a 'Delete' button (red border). The Create/Update button is disabled when the transition name is empty.

groups.name: State View Tab Content
groups.description: The State View tab renders the shared StateViewPanel component with a 2-pane layout: left sidebar (state list with search/filter and view toggle) and right detail panel. It supports List and Spatial view modes. Element thumbnails are passed through for visual display.

assertions.description: The states panel shows a 'States' heading with a count badge showing the total number of states
A search input with 'Filter states...' placeholder allows users to filter the state list by name
A List/Spatial view mode toggle allows switching between a text list view and a force-directed spatial canvas view of states
assertions.expected: The states panel should have two toggle buttons (List and Spatial/BarChart3 icons) that switch between a collapsible text list and a force-directed canvas view of state nodes

assertions.description: Clicking a state in the State View tab selects it and shows its details in the right panel
assertions.expected: Clicking a state row should select the state, deselect any transition, and display the state's details in the right panel of the StateViewPanel
preconditions: A config is selected with at least one state

assertions.description: When no state is selected, the detail area shows a placeholder message
assertions.expected: The right pane of the State View tab should show instructional text like 'Select a state to view its details' when no state is selected

groups.name: Transitions Tab Content
groups.description: The Transitions tab renders the shared TransitionsPanel component with a left sidebar (searchable transition list with state filters) and a right detail panel with action playback controls.

assertions.description: The transitions panel shows a 'Transitions' heading with a count badge showing the total number of transitions
A search input with 'Search transitions...' placeholder allows users to filter the transition list
Two state filter dropdowns ('All from states' and 'All target states') allow filtering transitions by source and destination states
assertions.expected: The transitions panel should have two dropdown filters: 'All from states' and 'All target states' that filter the transition list by source and destination states respectively

assertions.description: When a transition is selected, the detail panel shows 'Action Playback' controls with play/pause, step forward/back, reset, speed selector, and progress
assertions.expected: Selecting a transition should reveal an 'Action Playback' section with: speed dropdown (0.5x-4x), progress bar, control buttons (Reset, Step Back, Play/Pause, Step Forward), timeline dots for each action, and 'Action X of N' progress text
preconditions: A config is selected with transitions

assertions.description: Clicking a transition in the list selects it, deselects any state, and shows its details
assertions.expected: Clicking a transition row should select the transition, deselect any selected state, and display the transition's name, metadata, and action playback controls in the detail panel
preconditions: A config is selected with at least one transition

groups.name: Pathfinding Tab Content
groups.description: The Pathfinding tab renders the shared PathfindingPanel component. Users select 'From' and 'To' states from dropdowns, choose an algorithm (Dijkstra or BFS), and click 'Find Path'. Results show path steps or error messages. Found paths are highlighted on the graph when switching to Graph Editor tab.

assertions.description: The pathfinding panel shows a 'Pathfinding' heading
A 'From' dropdown allows users to select the starting state for pathfinding
assertions.expected: After finding a path with result.found === true, switching to the Graph Editor tab should show the path edges highlighted. If no path is found, highlightedPath is cleared.
preconditions: A config is selected with states and transitions

assertions.description: After finding a path, results show path steps or appropriate messages. Found paths are also highlighted on the graph.
assertions.expected: After clicking 'Find Path': (1) Success: shows path found with step count and total cost, listing each step with transition name and from-to states. (2) Same state: indicates already at target. (3) No path: shows no path found message.
preconditions: A config is selected with states

groups.name: Export Tab Content
groups.description: The Export tab renders the ExportPanel component, allowing users to save the active config to a JSON file or load a config from a JSON file. Shows the current config summary.

assertions.description: A save/export button allows saving the active config as a JSON file
assertions.expected: The Export tab should have a button to save/export the current config to a JSON file via Tauri's save dialog

assertions.description: A load/import button allows loading a config from a JSON file
assertions.expected: The Export tab should have a button to load/import a config from a JSON file via Tauri's open dialog

groups.name: Discovery Algorithm — State Grouping Correctness
groups.description: After running state discovery, the discovered states are verified for algorithmic correctness. The fingerprint-based discovery groups elements by co-occurrence patterns, position zones, and landmark context. These assertions can be verified on the state preview list (Phase 4) or after saving on the State View/Graph tabs.

assertions.description: Every discovered state has at least one element fingerprint. A state with zero elements indicates a grouping error in the discovery algorithm.
assertions.expected: After saving a discovery result and viewing the State View tab, every state in the list should display at least one element. On the discovery preview, every state row should appear with a name derived from its position zone (e.g., 'Header', 'Main Content', 'Footer').
preconditions: States are visible in State View or discovery preview

assertions.description: No two states should have identical element sets. If two states show the same elements, the discovery algorithm failed to merge them.
assertions.expected: Examining the element lists of all states (in State View tab detail panels), no two states should have identical sets of element IDs. Each state represents a distinct UI configuration.
preconditions: Discovery has completed and config saved

assertions.description: Each discovered state has a confidence score between 0 and 1, computed from observation frequency. States seen in more captures should have higher confidence.
assertions.expected: In the discovery preview, each state should display a confidence percentage (0-100%). States with fingerprints that appear in many captures should have higher confidence than states with rarely-seen fingerprints.

assertions.description: Fingerprints appearing in >80% of captures (e.g., persistent header/footer elements) should be identified as global states, separate from page-specific states.
assertions.expected: If the app has persistent elements (header, footer, navigation), the discovery result should create separate global states for these, distinguishable from page-specific content states. Global states are identified by fingerprints with >80% appearance rate across captures.
preconditions: Discovery completed from an app with persistent header/footer elements

groups.name: Loading States and Error Handling
groups.description: The page shows loading indicators during async operations and handles errors via toast notifications. A Loader2 spinner appears in the Graph Editor during config loading. The Refresh button's icon spins during loading. Toast notifications appear for save success/failure.

assertions.description: The Graph Editor tab shows a centered Loader2 spinner while config data is loading
assertions.expected: When sm.isLoading is true and the Graph Editor tab is active, a centered Loader2 spinner (size-8, animate-spin, brand-primary color) should be displayed instead of the graph content

assertions.description: The Refresh button's icon spins during loading and the button is disabled
assertions.expected: When isLoading is true, the RefreshCw icon in the Refresh button should have the animate-spin class and the button should be disabled (opacity-50)
preconditions: An async operation is in progress

assertions.description: Toast notifications appear for operation results (save success, save failure, drag-and-drop results)
assertions.expected: A ToastContainer renders toast notifications at the bottom of the page. Success toasts (green) appear after saving a config. Error toasts (red) appear when operations fail. Toasts can be dismissed.
preconditions: An operation has completed (success or failure)
